title: SGLang multimodal scheduler pickle deserialization permits remote code execution
ai_system: Antiproof AI-powered vulnerability discovery system (specific model not identified)
organization: Antiproof / SGLang maintainers (no vendor response recorded by CERT/CC)
summary: The multimodal generation runtime scheduler ROUTER socket deserializes incoming messages with pickle.loads(). Antiproof describes unauthenticated code execution when the scheduler socket is network-reachable. It states the socket follows --host, whose code default is 127.0.0.1, while some deployment examples use 0.0.0.0; CERT/CC instead states the scheduler binds to 0.0.0.0 by default. Scope the reachability/default discrepancy explicitly.
ai_role: The Antiproof article identifies this CVE as one of three findings it disclosed on 2026-03-10. Antiproof’s AI-system page explicitly includes CVE-2026-7301 in the system’s autonomously discovered and validated cases. Neither source names a model or describes the model’s individual investigative steps. CERT/CC independently records the pickle sink and conditional RCE impact.
classification_note: Public disclosure is documented by the Antiproof report and CERT/CC note. The checked sources do not establish exploitation in the wild; disclosure status does not imply it was or was not a zero-day.
remediation_note: Antiproof and CERT/CC report no official patch as of 2026-05-15 and 2026-05-18 respectively. Current remediation or fixed release boundary was not established by these checks.

impacts.conditions: Unauthenticated remote code execution as the SGLang process user when multimodal mode is enabled and the scheduler ROUTER socket is reachable. The source sources conflict about whether 0.0.0.0 is default; deployments using 127.0.0.1 do not expose the socket remotely absent other access.
impacts.exploitation: The cited sources describe vulnerability capability and conditions; they do not report observed exploitation in the wild.
